subject.title: fix: add emergency bypass for staged prepublication when worker is unavailable

question: Should staged prepublication checks ever be bypassable from publisher-controlled API/CLI input, or must emergency recovery stay server/operator-controlled?
rationale: This is a security boundary decision because the proposed public field skips prepublication scanners for untrusted published content.

options.title: Keep recovery operator-gated
options.body: Remove the public request field and recover stuck attempts through staff/admin tooling, a targeted maintenance action, or an operator-controlled deployment setting with auditability.

options.title: Narrow to authorized emergency use
options.body: Allow a bypass only after adding server-side staff/operator authorization, explicit audit logging, tests, and documentation of when it may be used.

options.title: Accept publisher bypass
options.body: Merge the public opt-out and document that publishers can skip prepublication checks when staging is enabled, accepting the weakened gate.

recommendation.title: Keep recovery operator-gated
recommendation.body: Remove the public request field and recover stuck attempts through staff/admin tooling, a targeted maintenance action, or an operator-controlled deployment setting with auditability.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the just-added staged prepublication implementation and worker path most directly affected by the boundary choice.
